description: Major depressive disorder, single episode, mild
content: ICD-10-CM F32.0: Major depressive disorder, single episode, mild. Maps to DSM-5 MDD mild specifier. 5 depressive symptoms, minor functional impairment.

description: Major depressive disorder, single episode, moderate
content: ICD-10-CM F32.1: Major depressive disorder, single episode, moderate. 6-7 symptoms, notable functional impairment across work and relationships.

description: Major depressive disorder, single episode, severe without psychotic features
content: ICD-10-CM F32.2: MDD single episode, severe without psychotic features. 8-9 symptoms, marked interference with daily functioning. Pharmacotherapy + psychotherapy indicated.

description: Major depressive disorder, single episode, severe with psychotic features
content: ICD-10-CM F32.3: MDD single episode, severe with psychotic features. Delusions or hallucinations present (mood-congruent or incongruent). Antipsychotic addition or ECT may be required.
ICD-10-CM F33.0: MDD recurrent episode, mild. Prior complete remission between episodes documented. Maintenance antidepressant therapy strongly recommended after 2+ episodes.
ICD-10-CM F33.1: MDD recurrent, moderate. Multiple prior episodes. Long-term maintenance therapy indicated. Assess for bipolar spectrum.

description: Major depressive disorder, recurrent, severe without psychotic features
content: ICD-10-CM F33.2: MDD recurrent, severe. Assess for treatment resistance. Consider augmentation strategies (lithium, atypicals, esketamine). Long-term prophylaxis essential.

description: Major depressive disorder, recurrent, severe with psychotic features
content: ICD-10-CM F33.3: MDD recurrent with psychotic features. Antidepressant + antipsychotic combination or ECT. High hospitalization risk.

description: Bipolar disorder, current episode manic without psychotic features
content: ICD-10-CM F31.1: Bipolar I disorder, current manic episode, without psychotic features. Mood stabilizer or atypical antipsychotic first-line. Avoid antidepressant monotherapy.

description: Bipolar disorder, current episode manic, severe, with psychotic features
content: ICD-10-CM F31.2: Bipolar I, manic with psychotic features. Antipsychotic + mood stabilizer combination. High hospitalization risk. Monitor for safety.

ICD-10-CM F31.81: Bipolar II disorder. Requires at least one hypomanic episode + one major depressive episode. Never had full manic episode. Lamotrigine and quetiapine evidence-based for bipolar II depression.
ICD-10-CM F41.1: Generalized Anxiety Disorder. Chronic excessive worry ≥6 months. SSRI/SNRI first-line. CBT evidence-based. Rule out thyroid dysfunction (TSH), caffeine, substances.
ICD-10-CM F41.0: Panic disorder, with or without agoraphobia. Recurrent unexpected panic attacks + persistent concern or behavioral changes. SSRI + CBT (panic control treatment) first-line.
ICD-10-CM F43.10: PTSD unspecified. Symptom duration >1 month. PE, CPT, EMDR first-line psychotherapy. Sertraline/paroxetine FDA-approved. Prazosin for nightmares.
ICD-10-CM F43.11: PTSD, acute (symptoms 1-3 months). Early intervention. Consider Acute Stress Disorder if <1 month.
ICD-10-CM F43.12: PTSD, chronic (>3 months). Long-term treatment planning. Assess comorbidities: MDD, SUD, chronic pain.
ICD-10-CM F20.9: Schizophrenia unspecified. Antipsychotic pharmacotherapy mandatory. Consider LAI for adherence. CSC program for first episode. Clozapine for treatment-resistant.
ICD-10-CM F60.3: Borderline Personality Disorder. DBT first-line psychological treatment. No FDA-approved medication. Target symptom clusters. Safety planning at every visit. Avoid benzodiazepines.
ICD-10-CM F90.2: ADHD combined presentation. Stimulants (methylphenidate, amphetamines) first-line. Non-stimulant (atomoxetine) if SUD concern. CBT adjunct for adults.

ICD-10-CM F42.2: OCD — obsessions and compulsions. ERP (Exposure and Response Prevention) gold standard. High-dose SSRIs first-line. 8-12 week trial needed. Augmentation: low-dose antipsychotic if partial response.

ICD-10-CM F10.20: Alcohol Use Disorder, moderate (4-5 criteria). FDA-approved medications: naltrexone 50 mg/day (reduces craving, monthly injectable Vivitrol available), acamprosate 666 mg TID (reduces withdrawal anxiety), disulfiram 250-500 mg/day (aversion — requires strict adherence). Psychosocial: CBT, MI, 12-step facilitation, SMART Recovery. CIWA-Ar scale for withdrawal monitoring. Thiamine supplementation mandatory to prevent Wernicke's encephalopathy.

ICD-10-CM F17.210: Nicotine dependence, cigarettes. First-line cessation: varenicline (Chantix) 0.5 mg/day × 3 days → 0.5 mg BID × 4 days → 1 mg BID for 12 weeks; most effective. NRT (patches, gum, lozenge); bupropion SR 150 mg BID. Combine pharmacotherapy + behavioral counseling for best outcomes.
